questions.q: What are the three states a CloudWatch alarm can be in?
options: OK, ALARM, and INSUFFICIENT_DATA
Active, Paused, and Deleted
Green, Yellow, and Red
Pending, Running, and Complete
questions.explain: An alarm continuously evaluates its metric against a threshold and sits in OK, ALARM, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA depending on whether the condition is met and whether enough data exists to judge.

questions.q: In the Lambda error-rate example, what does the alarm's action actually do?
options: Publishes a notification to an SNS topic that emails the on-call engineer
Automatically deletes the failing Lambda function
Silently logs the event with no further action
Increases the Lambda function's memory allocation
questions.explain: The alarm's configured action publishes to an SNS topic, which routes the notification to a human (or an automated remediation Lambda) subscribed to that topic.

questions.q: What is a CloudWatch dashboard for?
options: A customizable collection of widgets pulling metrics and logs from multiple services into one view
A tool that automatically fixes failing pipelines
A replacement for CloudWatch alarms
A place to store raw S3 objects
questions.explain: Dashboards combine widgets from any namespace or region into a single view, answering 'how is everything doing right now' rather than replacing alarm-driven notifications.

questions.q: Which AWS service is typically used to deliver a CloudWatch alarm's notification to a person?
options: SNS (Simple Notification Service)
S3 (Simple Storage Service)
IAM (Identity and Access Management)
Glue
questions.explain: SNS topics are the standard delivery mechanism for CloudWatch alarm actions — subscribers can receive email, SMS, or trigger further automation.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an alarm firing isn't the same as monitoring actually working?
options: Because an alarm without a notification action reaching someone provides little real value, even if it correctly transitions to ALARM
Because CloudWatch alarms cannot detect real failures
Because dashboards are required for an alarm to be valid
Because alarms automatically expire after one trigger
questions.explain: An alarm that transitions to ALARM but has no action attached — or an action nobody sees — fails to close the loop between detecting a problem and someone responding to it.
